title: Car Fleet
keyIdea: Compute each car's arrival time if alone: (target − position) / speed. Go from the car closest to the target backwards. If a car's time is greater than the fleet ahead's, it can never catch up: new fleet (push). Otherwise it joins that fleet. The answer is the number of fleets.

approaches.name: Sort + counter
approaches.idea: Same order and comparison, but keep only the latest fleet's arrival time in one variable instead of a stack.
approaches.why: Sorting dominates. Only the fleet directly ahead matters, so a single variable is enough; the pairs vector is still O(n).

approaches.name: Sort + stack of fleet times
approaches.idea: Sort by position, closest to the target first. Push a car's time only if it's greater than st.top(); st.size() is the number of fleets.
approaches.why: The sort is O(n log n); the loop is O(n) with at most one push per car.

quiz.q: Why go from the car closest to the target backwards?
options: A car can only be slowed by cars ahead of it, so those must be decided first
It's faster to sort that way

quiz.q: Why compare arrival times instead of speeds?
options: A fast car far behind can still arrive later; time combines distance and speed

quiz.q: A car's time equals the fleet ahead's time exactly. What happens?
options: It joins that fleet: they reach the target together, which counts as one fleet

quiz.q: Why isn't anything ever popped from the stack?
options: A joining car takes the fleet's slower time, so the top stays correct
